messages.content: Chicago update before I click purchase: the expo just made Sunday booth setup mandatory from about 3:30 to 6:30, and the Thursday West Loop client breakfast is confirmed for 8:00. My spouse can’t come, so the River North weekend idea is off. Can you reset the plan?

Yes. That pushes the outbound earlier and makes the return simpler. I would drop the Sunday afternoon arrival you were considering; landing close to setup leaves no room for O’Hare bags, traffic, or storms. Best path is a late-morning DEN to O’Hare nonstop, no rental car, South Loop or event-block hotel Sunday through Wednesday, and a Thursday early-afternoon ORD return after breakfast and checkout.
No rental. I’ll rideshare with the demo gear. Is Midway still worth looking at? It’s cheaper on one itinerary.

Only if the savings is big. Midway is workable, but it is less convenient for the convention area and it does not help the Thursday ORD return. Once you add extra transfer time and a rideshare with gear, a modest fare savings probably is not worth it.
The concrete outbound choices are: United nonstop 10:42 a.m. DEN-ORD landing 2:12, another ORD nonstop at 12:35 landing 3:54, or an 11:20 Midway flight about $80 cheaper.

Take the 10:42 to O’Hare. It is the only one that gives a real cushion before setup. The 12:35 landing at 3:54 is too close even if everything is on time, and Midway saves $80 while adding complexity right when you are carrying supplies.
Good. Return Thursday from ORD: 12:05, 1:45, or 3:10. Breakfast should be done by 9:30, but I need to get back to the hotel and check out.

I would skip 12:05. It forces a rushed hotel stop and airport transfer. The 1:45 is the clean pick: enough time for breakfast, checkout, and O’Hare security without sitting around all afternoon. The 3:10 is your backup if the breakfast is likely to run long.

Let’s do 1:45. Hotel choice: event block is closest, but it only has a higher-rate two-queen room and almost no amenities. South Loop can hold a quiet king, has pool and fitness, no listed hot tub, and reviews are around 4.3.

South Loop still sounds like the better booking. The event block wins on walk time, but you would pay more for a room type you do not need and weaker recovery options. Since you are ridesharing for airport and gear moves anyway, the extra walk or short ride from South Loop is manageable.
I can live without the hot tub for this one. Is South Loop a problem for the West Loop breakfast?

No. For Thursday, go to breakfast with just your work bag if possible, return to the hotel by about 10:15, then check out and request a car to O’Hare around 10:45 to 11:00. If the hotel offers noon checkout at no charge, take it, but the plan does not depend on it.
Okay. Drop the extension completely and give me the booking checklist.

Book these pieces: 1) DEN-ORD Sunday 10:42 a.m. nonstop and ORD-DEN Thursday 1:45 p.m.; choose window seats if available, especially on the return before the seat map fills. 2) South Loop hotel Sunday through Wednesday nights, checkout Thursday; request a quiet king away from elevators, upper floor if available, and note pool plus fitness confirmed but no hot tub listed. 3) Do not hold River North or spouse travel. Release the event block unless it is penalty-free and you want a one-day backup. 4) Transit: rideshare or taxi ORD to hotel/convention, no rental; keep the convention address and setup entrance pinned separately. 5) Expense notes: save airfare, hotel cancellation terms, block-rate comparison, rideshare receipts, and a short note that South Loop was lower cost than the remaining block room while providing the needed room type.

messages.content: Chicago leaves in five days. I booked the 10:42 Sunday nonstop into O’Hare, the 1:45 Thursday return, and the South Loop hotel. The expo app now says badge pickup is in Hall F, but booth setup entrance is Hall B. Also, Blue Line work and Sunday storms are both showing up.

The itinerary still works, but I would not depend on the train from O’Hare that day. Plan a taxi or rideshare from ORD. If you land around 2:12, aim to be in the car by 2:50 and at the hotel or convention area by about 3:45, with setup paperwork ready in case storms slow arrivals.
I’m bringing one demo roller and a backpack, not a big checked case.

Good. Keep the roller with you if it fits the aircraft limits; if you have to gate-check it, go straight to baggage claim and skip the hotel before setup. With Hall F badge pickup and Hall B setup, screenshot both maps and put the QR code somewhere accessible offline.
Hotel confirmed room away from elevators, pool and fitness access, still no hot tub.
That is fine for this trip. Save the confirmation email with the room note and amenities, and set a reminder to ask at check-in about any lap-swim hours or fitness-room access limits.
Thursday breakfast is 8 in the West Loop. Checkout is 11 unless I ask.

Pack most things Wednesday night. Thursday morning, take only your work bag to breakfast, return to the hotel by 10:15, check out by 10:45, and leave for O’Hare no later than 11. If they grant noon checkout, treat it as cushion, not a reason to linger.
Return seat map shifted after an aircraft swap. My outbound window is still set; return has only middle seats open right now.

Keep the current return seat for now and check again at 72 hours, 24 hours, and at check-in; aircraft swaps often release windows later. Packing: compact work bag with laptop, charger, hotspot, clicker, badge QR screenshot, printed setup notes, glasses/meds, snacks, empty bottle, small umbrella or rain shell, and a receipts envelope. Wear shoes you can stand in for setup, and keep one clean top in the backpack in case storms delay your bag or arrival.

messages.content: Chicago is finally off my desk. I have a late-August Pacific Northwest clinic rollout now, and it is one of those four-city zigzags. Can you help me build the first flight/hotel/car plan before I start clicking?
Absolutely. Give me the fixed stops and anything still pending. I especially need the first required time, the last required time, whether Friday is real, and how much training gear you are carrying.

Fixed so far: Monday afternoon handoff near Vancouver, Washington; Tuesday training on Portland’s east side; Wednesday session in Salem; Thursday hands-on lab in Eugene. Friday debrief in Portland is not confirmed. I’ll have the demo roller and probably one box of supplies.

First read: use Portland as the entry point, not Eugene. Flying into Eugene first would create backtracking before Vancouver and Portland. With supplies, I’d also plan on a rental car from PDX and avoid downtown hotels unless there is a meeting there.
Yes, easy parking matters more than restaurants. I can handle one hotel move, but I don’t want a silly drive on a training morning.

Then the clean shape is Portland area Sunday through Tuesday, move south after the Salem session Wednesday, and use Eugene for the Thursday lab. Portland-only is simpler for packing, but it creates a long Thursday morning drive before the hands-on lab.
For flights, I saw a Sunday afternoon DEN-PDX nonstop, and a Monday morning one-stop that is about $160 cheaper. The Monday flight gets in late morning if nothing slips.

I would choose the Sunday afternoon nonstop. The Monday one-stop is cheaper, but it is fragile for a Monday afternoon handoff: one delay or missed connection turns into a scramble with supplies. Sunday gives you time to land, get the car, check the equipment, and sleep in Portland before the first stop.
Agreed. No reason to start that week stressed. What rental class?

Book a small SUV or midsize crossover at PDX, not a compact sedan. You want a flat cargo area for the roller and box, plus enough room to keep the cabin organized. Use a PDX round-trip rental for now; only change to a one-way Eugene drop if Friday debrief is canceled and the math still works.

Hotel options I found: eastside Portland property rated about 4.4, pool and fitness, no hot tub, free parking; downtown Portland 4.6 and better food, but $48 parking; Eugene hotel 4.5 with pool, hot tub, fitness, and free parking.

Rank them this way: 1) eastside Portland for Sunday-Tuesday because it matches Tuesday’s location, keeps parking easy, and still has pool and fitness. 2) Eugene hotel for Wednesday and possibly Thursday because it reduces the Thursday lab commute and has the better recovery amenities. 3) downtown Portland only if Friday debrief lands downtown and they cover parking, because it is otherwise the least practical.
Would you keep the same Portland hotel the whole week just to avoid moving?

I would not for this route. Staying Portland-only means Portland to Salem Wednesday, back to Portland, then Portland to Eugene Thursday morning, and potentially back again Friday. One hotel move after Salem saves the worst drive and lowers the chance that Thursday starts late.
If Friday debrief happens in Portland, should I drive back Thursday night after the Eugene lab?

Only if the debrief is early Friday and the Thursday lab ends at a reasonable hour. If the debrief is 11 a.m. or later, sleep in Eugene Thursday and drive up Friday morning. If they set an 8:30 a.m. Portland debrief, switch Thursday night to a Portland airport or eastside hotel instead of doing a tired late-night drive.
Let’s assume the debrief is around 11, but not confirmed. Which return city should I plan around?

Plan around PDX for now. It has better nonstop options to Denver and keeps the rental simple as a PDX round trip. If Friday debrief disappears, compare two backups: Friday late-morning Eugene departure with a connection, or drive back to PDX for an afternoon nonstop. I would not lock a nonrefundable return until Friday is confirmed.
Can I safely book the Sunday outbound now and wait on the return?

Yes, if the fare rules allow a one-way or changeable booking that your company accepts. Book the Sunday afternoon DEN-PDX nonstop now. For the return, either hold a changeable Friday afternoon PDX-DEN or wait until the debrief decision date, but put a reminder on the calendar so fares do not drift too long.
Equipment handling: I don’t want supplies sitting in a hot car all afternoon between stops.

Ship the extra box to the Monday handoff site or the Portland hotel if they will accept it. Keep the demo roller with you. During clinic days, park in shade or covered parking when available, bring temperature-sensitive pieces inside, and do not leave branded gear visible overnight. Ask each site about loading doors so you are not dragging the roller through public entrances.
What confirmations do I need from the clinics before I book the hotels?

Confirm these before final hotel commitments: exact Monday handoff address and start/end window near Vancouver; Tuesday eastside Portland parking and room access time; Wednesday Salem end time and whether you can leave directly south afterward; Thursday Eugene lab start/end time, loading access, and whether supplies can stay onsite during breaks; Friday debrief yes/no, location, and earliest possible start. First plan to hold: Sunday afternoon DEN-PDX nonstop, PDX small SUV round trip, eastside Portland hotel Sunday-Tuesday, refundable Eugene hotel Wednesday-Thursday with Thursday adjustable, and likely Friday afternoon PDX-DEN if the debrief is confirmed. After booking flights, pick a window seat if one is open and keep the demo roller out of bulkhead rows if you need under-seat access.
